root=Column([a,d,h,i,k,l,m,q,r,w,x,ag],"md",padding=16)
a=Column([b,c],"sm")
b=Text("App permissions","h2")
c=Text("iOS asks for sensitive permissions when an app needs them, not at install time, and lets you decide per feature such as location, contacts, photos, microphone, and Bluetooth.[2][15]","caption")
d=Column([e,f,g],"sm")
e=Text("Android also uses runtime permissions on modern versions, but the interface is more device-dependent; users typically review permissions in the Location or Permission Manager screens and can switch access off per app.[3][14]","caption")
f=Text("In practice, both platforms now support granular controls, but iOS is usually described as more consistent and clearer in how it presents those choices.","caption")
g=Text("Approximate location","h2")
h=Text("iOS lets you choose Precise Location on or off for each app, so you can share only an approximate area when exact coordinates are unnecessary.","caption")
i=Column([j],"sm")
j=Text("Android location controls are usually organized around whether an app may access location at all, plus system location services and app-level permission toggles; some Android guidance also refers to background, while-in-use, and deny options depending on device and version.[6][10]","caption")
k=Text("For broad privacy, both systems also allow turning location services off at the device level, which stops apps from using the phone’s location altogether.","caption")
l=Text("Android does not provide the same app-tracking prompt model in the cited sources, but it does offer controls for app location permissions and related location-history features through Google or device settings.[12]","caption")
m=Column([n,o],"sm")
n=Text("Tracking controls","h2")
o=Column([p],"sm")
p=Text("iOS includes a Tracking setting that lets you block apps from requesting tracking, and it can also prompt about ongoing location access in a way that is easy to review later.[13]","caption")
q=Text("On both platforms, the strongest control is to deny unnecessary location access and limit apps to while using where possible.","caption")
r=Column([s,t],"sm")
s=Text("Privacy reports","h2")
t=Column([u,v],"sm")
u=Text("Apple provides a Privacy Report feature in newer iOS versions that summarizes how often apps access sensors and network domains, helping users audit app behavior; this feature is distinct from the location permission screen.","caption")
v=Text("The supplied Android sources do not show an equivalent built-in privacy report with the same scope and presentation, although Android does provide per-app permission history and location-related settings on many devices.","caption")
w=Text("Because device vendors and OS versions vary, the exact report features on Android can differ more than on iPhone.[9]","caption")
x=Column([y,z],"sm")
y=Text("Practical settings checklist","h2")
z=Column([aa,ab,ac,ad,ae,af],"sm")
aa=Text("Review Location permissions for every app and remove access that is not needed.","caption")
ab=Text("Set maps, rideshare, delivery, and weather apps to While Using or equivalent, not Always.","caption")
ac=Text("Turn Precise Location off on iPhone for apps that only need an approximate area.","caption")
ad=Text("Disable device-wide location services when they are not needed.","caption")
ae=Text("Check tracking permissions on iPhone and block apps from requesting tracking unless you trust the app.","caption")
af=Text("Review related location history or system location features tied to Google or Apple accounts.","caption")
ag=Column([ah,ai],"sm")
ah=Text("Limits of these controls","h2")
ai=Column([aj,ak,al,am],"sm")
aj=Text("Permission systems reduce exposure, but they do not guarantee that an app cannot infer location through other signals such as IP address, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or account activity.","caption")
ak=Text("Some apps will not function fully if you restrict core permissions, so privacy often involves a trade-off with app features.","caption")
al=Text("Vendor and OS differences matter: Android controls can vary by phone maker and version, while iOS controls are more standardized across devices.","caption")
am=Text("A permission denial also does not erase data already collected, so account-level privacy settings and data deletion controls still matter.","caption")
</a2ui>

<a2ui>
root=Column([a,b,c,e,g,i,j,q,r,s,u],"md",padding=16)
a=Text("Everyday stress vs burnout","h2")
b=Text("Everyday work stress is a response to pressure that may still feel manageable, while occupational burnout is a syndrome that develops after chronic workplace stress has not been successfully managed. The World Health Organization describes burnout by three features: energy depletion or exhaustion, increased mental distance or negativism toward one’s job, and reduced professional efficacy, and it says burnout applies to the occupational context rather than life in general [1]. Mayo Clinic notes that burnout is not a medical diagnosis and can overlap with other conditions such as depression, which is why persistent symptoms deserve attention.","body")
c=Card([d])
d=Text("Common signs","h2")
e=Card([f])
f=Text("Stress often shows up as feeling tense, worried, irritable, or temporarily overloaded, but burnout tends to feel deeper and more persistent, with emotional exhaustion, detachment, and a sense of not accomplishing much [6]. Common burnout signs include dragging yourself to work, cynicism, low patience, trouble concentrating, reduced satisfaction, sleep changes, headaches, stomach issues, and using food, alcohol, or drugs to cope [13]. NHS guidance also highlights feeling tired and drained, losing motivation, feeling helpless or detached, becoming more negative, withdrawing from others, and struggling to get things done.","body")
g=Card([h])
h=Text("One-week coping routine","h2")
i=Text("Day 5: Ask one trusted person for support and talk through what feels hardest.","body")
j=Column([k,l,m,n,o,p],"sm")
k=Text("Day 1: Write down the top 3 work stressors and 1 thing you can pause or delegate this week.","body")
l=Text("Day 2: Set a firm start and stop time for work, and protect a real break away from screens.","body")
m=Text("Day 3: Use 10 minutes of movement, such as a walk or stretching, to interrupt tension.","body")
n=Text("Day 4: Try one calming practice, such as slow breathing, mindfulness, or meditation, for 5 to 10 minutes.","body")
o=Text("Day 6: Review sleep habits and aim for a consistent bedtime and wake time.","body")
p=Text("Day 7: Reassess your workload and decide what needs a manager conversation or longer-term change.","body")
q=Text("Workplace changes that help","h2")
r=Text("Helpful changes usually address the source of stress, not just the symptoms. Mayo Clinic recommends discussing workload, expectations, control over tasks, conflicts, and work-life balance with a manager, while also setting realistic goals and clarifying what can wait. In practice, useful changes include reducing overload, improving schedule control, clarifying priorities, adding support, and making it easier to take breaks and disconnect after work.","body")
s=Card([t])
t=Text("When to get support","h2")
u=Text("Professional support may help if symptoms last more than a short period, interfere with daily life, or start affecting sleep, mood, or physical health. It is especially important to seek help if you feel hopeless, cannot function at work, are relying on alcohol or drugs to cope, or think the problem might be depression or another mental health condition. NHS guidance says to speak with a GP or contact talking therapies if burnout is affecting daily life or mental health.","body")
v=Card([q])
</a2ui>

a=Text("What to keep as evidence","h2")
b=Text("Save the order confirmation, invoice/bill, product listing screenshots, and payment proof.","body")
c=Card([d])
d=Column([e,f,g,h],"sm")
e=Text("Take photos or videos of the defect, ideally during unboxing, and keep the packaging, labels, and accessories.","body")
f=Column([g,h,i,j],"sm")
g=Text("Preserve all emails, chat logs, complaint ticket numbers, pickup receipts, and return/refund status updates.","body")
h=Text("If the product was inspected or repaired, keep any job sheet or written service report.","body")
i=Text("First complaint: seller and platform","h2")
j=Text("Report the defect immediately in writing through the app, email, or seller support, and clearly ask for refund, replacement, or repair.","body")
k=Card([l])
l=Column([m,n,o],"sm")
m=Text("If the marketplace route fails, escalate to the platform’s grievance officer/nodal contact and include the order number, defect details, evidence, and the exact remedy sought.","body")
n=Text("Under current consumer guidance, platform-side redressal should be triggered quickly; some guidance cites a 72-hour response expectation for defective goods, but this should be treated as a platform-facing service timeline rather than a guaranteed statutory remedy window.","body")
o=Text("Official grievance channels","h2")
p=Text("Use the National Consumer Helpline (NCH) as the pre-litigation escalation step; official consumer guidance lists 1915 as the toll-free helpline, with online and app-based complaint options.","body")
q=Text("File the grievance with enough detail so the complaint can be forwarded and tracked: seller name, platform name, order ID, issue summary, evidence list, and the remedy requested.","body")
r=Card([s])
s=Column([t,u,v],"sm")
t=Text("Escalation if the issue is not resolved","h2")
u=Text("If the seller/platform does not resolve the matter, file a complaint on e-Daakhil for the appropriate Consumer Commission.","body")
v=Text("Choose the commission based on the value and jurisdiction of the claim; current consumer-law guides direct consumers to the District, State, or National Commission through the online filing system.","body")
w=Card([x])
x=Column([y,z,aa],"sm")
y=Text("Deadlines and timing","h2")
z=Text("The consumer complaint limitation period is generally 2 years from the cause of action under the Consumer Protection Act framework and related guidance.","body")
aa=Text("Act as soon as the defect is discovered, because delay can weaken evidence and make platform reversals harder to obtain.","body")
ab=Card([ac])
ac=Column([ad,ae,af],"sm")
ad=Text("Practical approach","h2")
ae=Text("Keep the defective item safe until the dispute is resolved, because the seller or platform may require inspection or return.","body")
af=Text("Use written communication only where possible, since a clear paper trail helps at every escalation stage.","body")
ag=Text("If the seller offers only store credit or a voucher for a clearly defective product, you can still press for the statutory remedy you want through the grievance and consumer-forum process.","body")
ah=Button("Continue","borderless",onPress=openUrl("https://www.consumerprotection.gov.au"))
</a2ui>

f=Text("Gene therapy commonly uses viral vectors, especially adeno-associated virus and lentiviral systems, because they efficiently carry therapeutic DNA into cells.","caption")
g=Text("This delivery approach can cause immunogenic toxicity and, with integrating vectors, insertional oncogenesis.","caption")
h=Text("CRISPR can be delivered by viral vectors, lipid nanoparticles, or by direct delivery of Cas protein and guide RNA as a ribonucleoprotein complex; the core challenge is getting the editing machinery into the right cells long enough to act.","caption")
i=Text("Established clinical examples","h2")
j=Text("Approved gene therapy includes several established products for inherited disease and hematologic disorders, such as AAV-based gene replacement and lentiviral ex vivo modification; these are now standard clinical categories rather than experimental concepts.","caption")

o=Text("CRISPR offers site-specific editing, but limitations include off-target edits, incomplete editing, dependence on repair pathways, and difficulty achieving uniform correction in all target cells.","caption")

v=Text("Approved today: conventional gene therapies and some somatic CRISPR therapies.","caption")
w=Text("Experimental or highly restricted: embryo editing, germline editing, enhancement applications, and many in vivo CRISPR programs still in trials.","caption")

root=Column([a,d,h,i,k,l,m,q,r,w,x,ag],"md",padding=16)
a=Column([b,c],"sm")
b=Text("App permissions","h2")
c=Text("iOS asks for sensitive permissions when an app needs them, not at install time, and lets you decide per feature such as location, contacts, photos, microphone, and Bluetooth.[2][15]","caption")
d=Column([e,f,g],"sm")
e=Text("Android also uses runtime permissions on modern versions, but the interface is more device-dependent; users typically review permissions in the Location or Permission Manager screens and can switch access off per app.[3][14]","caption")
f=Text("In practice, both platforms now support granular controls, but iOS is usually described as more consistent and clearer in how it presents those choices.","caption")
g=Text("Approximate location","h2")
h=Text("iOS lets you choose Precise Location on or off for each app, so you can share only an approximate area when exact coordinates are unnecessary.","caption")
i=Column([j],"sm")
j=Text("Android location controls are usually organized around whether an app may access location at all, plus system location services and app-level permission toggles; some Android guidance also refers to background, while-in-use, and deny options depending on device and version.[6][10]","caption")
k=Text("For broad privacy, both systems also allow turning location services off at the device level, which stops apps from using the phone’s location altogether.","caption")
l=Text("Android does not provide the same app-tracking prompt model in the cited sources, but it does offer controls for app location permissions and related location-history features through Google or device settings.[12]","caption")
m=Column([n,o],"sm")
n=Text("Tracking controls","h2")
o=Column([p],"sm")
p=Text("iOS includes a Tracking setting that lets you block apps from requesting tracking, and it can also prompt about ongoing location access in a way that is easy to review later.[13]","caption")
q=Text("On both platforms, the strongest control is to deny unnecessary location access and limit apps to while using where possible.","caption")
r=Column([s,t],"sm")
s=Text("Privacy reports","h2")
t=Column([u,v],"sm")
u=Text("Apple provides a Privacy Report feature in newer iOS versions that summarizes how often apps access sensors and network domains, helping users audit app behavior; this feature is distinct from the location permission screen.","caption")
v=Text("The supplied Android sources do not show an equivalent built-in privacy report with the same scope and presentation, although Android does provide per-app permission history and location-related settings on many devices.","caption")
w=Text("Because device vendors and OS versions vary, the exact report features on Android can differ more than on iPhone.[9]","caption")
x=Column([y,z],"sm")
y=Text("Practical settings checklist","h2")
z=Column([aa,ab,ac,ad,ae,af],"sm")
aa=Text("Review Location permissions for every app and remove access that is not needed.","caption")
ab=Text("Set maps, rideshare, delivery, and weather apps to While Using or equivalent, not Always.","caption")
ac=Text("Turn Precise Location off on iPhone for apps that only need an approximate area.","caption")
ad=Text("Disable device-wide location services when they are not needed.","caption")
ae=Text("Check tracking permissions on iPhone and block apps from requesting tracking unless you trust the app.","caption")
af=Text("Review related location history or system location features tied to Google or Apple accounts.","caption")
ag=Column([ah,ai],"sm")
ah=Text("Limits of these controls","h2")
ai=Column([aj,ak,al,am],"sm")
aj=Text("Permission systems reduce exposure, but they do not guarantee that an app cannot infer location through other signals such as IP address, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or account activity.","caption")
ak=Text("Some apps will not function fully if you restrict core permissions, so privacy often involves a trade-off with app features.","caption")
al=Text("Vendor and OS differences matter: Android controls can vary by phone maker and version, while iOS controls are more standardized across devices.","caption")
am=Text("A permission denial also does not erase data already collected, so account-level privacy settings and data deletion controls still matter.","caption")
</a2ui>

a=Text("What to keep as evidence","h2")
b=Text("Save the order confirmation, invoice/bill, product listing screenshots, and payment proof.\nTake photos or videos of the defect, ideally during unboxing, and keep the packaging, labels, and accessories.\nPreserve all emails, chat logs, complaint ticket numbers, pickup receipts, and return/refund status updates.\nIf the product was inspected or repaired, keep any job sheet or written service report.","body")
c=Text("First complaint: seller and platform","h2")
d=Text("Report the defect immediately in writing through the app, email, or seller support, and clearly ask for refund, replacement, or repair.\nIf the marketplace route fails, escalate to the platform’s grievance officer/nodal contact and include the order number, defect details, evidence, and the exact remedy sought.","body")
e=Text("Under current consumer guidance, platform-side redressal should be triggered quickly; some guidance cites a 72-hour response expectation for defective goods, but this should be treated as a platform-facing service timeline rather than a guaranteed statutory remedy window.","caption")
f=Text("Official grievance channels","h2")
g=Text("Use the National Consumer Helpline (NCH) as the pre-litigation escalation step; official consumer guidance lists 1915 as the toll-free helpline, with online and app-based complaint options.","caption")
h=Text("File the grievance with enough detail so the complaint can be forwarded and tracked: seller name, platform name, order ID, issue summary, evidence list, and the remedy requested.","caption")
i=Text("Escalation if the issue is not resolved","h2")
j=Text("If the seller/platform does not resolve the matter, file a complaint on e-Daakhil for the appropriate Consumer Commission. Choose the commission based on the value and jurisdiction of the claim; current consumer-law guides direct consumers to the District, State, or National Commission through the online filing system.","caption")
k=Text("In the complaint, name both the seller and, where relevant, the platform, and request refund/replacement/repair, compensation, and costs.","caption")
l=Text("Deadlines and timing","h2")
m=Text("The consumer complaint limitation period is generally 2 years from the cause of action under the Consumer Protection Act framework and related guidance.\nAct as soon as the defect is discovered, because delay can weaken evidence and make platform reversals harder to obtain.\nIf you paid by card and the refund is wrongly withheld, some consumer guidance notes that a bank chargeback may be tried in parallel, subject to your card issuer’s timelines.","caption")
n=Text("Practical approach","h2")
o=Text("Keep the defective item safe until the dispute is resolved, because the seller or platform may require inspection or return.\nUse written communication only where possible, since a clear paper trail helps at every escalation stage.\nIf the seller offers only store credit or a voucher for a clearly defective product, you can still press for the statutory remedy you want through the grievance and consumer-forum process.","caption")
</a2ui>

a=Column([b,c],"sm")
b=Text("Mechanism","h2")
c=Text("Gene therapy treats disease by delivering a therapeutic gene, or by replacing, supplementing, or silencing a faulty gene; it does not necessarily cut the genome at a specific DNA sequence.[2][14]","caption")
d=Column([e,f],"sm")
e=Text("CRISPR gene editing uses a guide RNA to bring a Cas nuclease to a chosen DNA site, where it creates a double-strand break; repair by NHEJ often disrupts a gene, while HDR can make a precise sequence change.","caption")
f=Text("In practice, CRISPR is a gene-editing platform that can be used inside a gene-therapy strategy, but the terms are not interchangeable.","caption")
g=Column([h,i,j],"sm")
h=Text("Gene therapy commonly uses viral vectors, especially adeno-associated virus and lentiviral systems, because they efficiently carry therapeutic DNA into cells.","caption")
i=Text("This delivery approach can cause immunogenic toxicity and, with integrating vectors, insertional oncogenesis.","caption")
j=Text("CRISPR can be delivered by viral vectors, lipid nanoparticles, or by direct delivery of Cas protein and guide RNA as a ribonucleoprotein complex; the core challenge is getting the editing machinery into the right cells long enough to act.","caption")
k=Column([l],"sm")
l=Text("Delivery methods","h2")
m=Column([n,o],"sm")
n=Text("By contrast, germline CRISPR editing of embryos or reproductive cells is not an approved clinical treatment and remains broadly restricted.[3][10]","caption")
o=Text("Limitations","h2")
p=Column([q,r],"sm")
q=Text("Established clinical examples","h2")
r=Column([s,t],"sm")
s=Text("Approved gene therapy includes several established products for inherited disease and hematologic disorders, such as AAV-based gene replacement and lentiviral ex vivo modification; these are now standard clinical categories rather than experimental concepts.","caption")
t=Text("Approved CRISPR-based therapy is now also a reality: ex vivo CRISPR editing of patient cells has reached clinical approval in some regions for severe hemoglobin disorders, showing that CRISPR is no longer limited to research.","caption")
u=Column([v,w,x],"sm")
v=Text("Gene therapy may give durable benefit, but it can be limited by immune responses, vector size constraints, and imperfect control of where and how strongly the added gene is expressed.","caption")
w=Text("CRISPR offers site-specific editing, but limitations include off-target edits, incomplete editing, dependence on repair pathways, and difficulty achieving uniform correction in all target cells.","caption")
x=Text("Both approaches face major delivery barriers, but CRISPR adds an extra layer of risk because a cut can create unintended DNA changes rather than simply adding a gene.","caption")
y=Column([z,aa,ab],"sm")
z=Text("Ethical questions","h2")
aa=Column([ab,ac],"sm")
ab=Text("For somatic treatments, ethics focuses mainly on safety, efficacy, informed consent, and fair access.[6][7]","caption")
ac=Text("For germline editing, the concerns become sharper: future people cannot consent, edits may be inherited, and there are worries about unpredictable harms, enhancement uses, and eugenics.[8][12]","caption")
ad=Column([ae,af],"sm")
ae=Text("Approved today: conventional gene therapies and some somatic CRISPR therapies.","caption")
af=Text("Experimental or highly restricted: embryo editing, germline editing, enhancement applications, and many in vivo CRISPR programs still in trials.","caption")
ag=Column([ah],"sm")
ah=Text("Approved vs. experimental","h2")
</a2ui>
